name: Medical image analysis (Chunliang Wang)
summary: Works on medical image analysis, image segmentation, machine learning with a focus on deep learning, and statistical shape modelling.
students: The profile does not say whether MSc theses are offered. Ask directly.

name: Computational medical image analysis (Rodrigo Moreno)
topics: Cancer imaging (DBT, 3D ultrasound, PET, CT, MRI)
summary: Builds mathematically founded tools for medical images: brain MR elastography in Parkinson's, Alzheimer's and brain tumours; AI to make diffusion MRI tractography more specific; AI-based registration that simulates how a brain MRI would look at other ages; and AI for 3D cancer imaging.
students: The profile lists courses but no thesis information. Ask directly.

name: Physics of Medical Imaging
pi: Mats Danielsson, Professor (heads the Hardware Development Group)
summary: Develops new medical imaging hardware together with image and signal processing, statistical models and machine learning built for clinical use. Its photon-counting CT system with a silicon detector is being verified in a clinical study at MedTechLabs, BioClinicum.
students: Yes. The group site lists MSc and PhD projects in medical imaging and invites thesis students.

name: Photon-counting CT reconstruction (Mats Persson)
unit: KTH SCI, with the Physics of Medical Imaging group
summary: Develops next-generation reconstruction methods for photon-counting CT, including a deep-learning method that cuts image noise (with KTH Mathematics) and a correction for physical effects that cause artefacts (with GE Research).
students: A PDF of MSc thesis projects in photon-counting CT is posted on KTH's file server. Open it to see current topics.

sources.label: KTH project: reconstruction methods for photon-counting CT
MSc thesis projects in photon-counting CT (PDF)

name: Deep learning under uncertainty (Hossein Azizpour)
unit: Robotics, Perception and Learning, KTH EECS; affiliated with SciLifeLab
summary: Research tracks on deep learning under uncertainty and weak supervision, interpretability, feature selection and generative or foundation models. Life-science applications include breast cancer risk prediction from mammograms (the CSAW-M dataset) and vision transformers on echocardiography.
students: No thesis information on the page. Contact him directly.

sources.label: PhD position: generative modelling of brain imaging (closed March 2026)

name: Computer Vision and Biomedical Image Analysis (Kevin Smith)
summary: Machine learning for medicine and biology. The group's AI systems have been tested in real-world clinical trials for cancer screening. Kevin Smith also directs the BioImage Informatics Facility node in Solna and works with Karolinska clinicians and AstraZeneca.
students: Yes. KTH students interested in an MSc thesis may contact him. Suggested areas: medical image classification and segmentation, microscopy denoising or super-resolution, outlier detection, risk prediction.

sources.label: Machine Learning and Computational Biology, KTH

name: Inverse problems and tomography (Ozan Öktem)
summary: Develops methods for inverse problems that combine deep learning with classical applied mathematics, applied to low-dose tomography and 3D electron microscopy of proteins.
students: Not stated. Ask directly.

name: Contrast-enhanced imaging and therapy (Dmitry Grishenkov)
unit: Biomedical Imaging, Dept. of Biomedical Engineering and Health Systems, KTH
summary: Characterises multimodal contrast agents and develops ways to image and quantify them, including a tissue-specific contrast agent for diagnostics and local drug delivery (with Karolinska Institutet) and microbubbles in lab-on-chip set-ups.
students: Yes. The group has supervised MSc theses most years since 2016, for example a 2024 thesis using GANs to improve low-frequency ultrasound images.

name: Quantitative ultrasound (Matilda Larsson)
pi: Matilda Larsson, Professor of Medical Image Processing
summary: Develops and validates quantitative ultrasound methods for cardiovascular and obstetric use, including shear wave elastography to measure tissue elasticity.
students: She is examiner for the Medical Engineering degree project (HL205X). Thesis topics are not listed on the page.

name: Signal processing and ML for health (Saikat Chatterjee)
unit: Information Science and Engineering, KTH EECS
summary: Signal processing and machine learning for detection, estimation and prediction. Lists 'AI for Health Care' and medical data analytics as a focus, and is a visiting researcher at Karolinska Institutet and Karolinska Hospital. A 2023 PhD thesis in the group studied deep learning for neonatal sepsis detection.
students: Not stated. Ask directly.

name: Live super-resolution microscopy (Ilaria Testa)
summary: Combines physics, biology and chemistry to build next-generation fluorescence microscopes that image living cells at super-resolution with less light damage, and uses them to study proteins in living, firing neurons.
students: No student information on the group page.

name: Neuronics: injury biomechanics (Xiaogai Li, Svein Kleiven)
unit: School of Engineering Sciences in Chemistry, Biotechnology and Health, KTH
summary: Combines AI with finite element human body models to personalise them, place them in realistic seated postures and reconstruct real accidents from images and video. Funded by Vinnova with Autoliv.
students: A PhD position is open now (see Jobs).

name: Robotics, Perception and Learning
pi: Contact on current posting: Danica Kragic Jensfelt
unit: Division of Robotics, Perception and Learning, KTH EECS
summary: Develops and evaluates robotic systems through hands-on experiments. A part-time research engineer role is open now.
students: A 50% research engineer role is open now (see Jobs).

sources.label: Research Engineer in Robotics, Perception and Learning

name: Predictive Medicine (Mattias Rantalainen)
unit: Medical Epidemiology and Biostatistics (MEB), Karolinska Institutet
summary: AI-based computational pathology for cancer precision medicine: deep learning on histopathology whole-slide images combined with DNA/RNA sequencing, clinical data and large population datasets. Co-developed an AI tool that refines breast tumour grading (Annals of Oncology, 2021).
students: Not stated on the group page.

sources.label: KI news: AI improves precision in breast cancer diagnosis (2021)

name: Precision Cancer Control (Martin Eklund)
unit: Medical Epidemiology and Biostatistics (MEB), Karolinska Institutet
summary: Combines biomarkers, genomics and medical imaging with statistics and AI to lower prostate and breast cancer mortality, and tests the methods in clinical trials. Includes an AI system that helps pathologists grade prostate biopsies, and MRI-based prostate screening.
students: Not stated on the group page.

name: Computational pathology and AI (Kimmo Kartasalo)
unit: Medical Epidemiology and Biostatistics (MEB), Karolinska Institutet; SciLifeLab
summary: AI for computational pathology in cancer: decision-support tools for pathologists and models combining image, molecular and clinical data to guide prognosis and therapy.
students: The computational pathology and AI group at MEB has an hourly research-assistant role open now that mentions possible degree projects (see Jobs).

sources.label: Research Assistant in AI for prostate cancer diagnostics

name: Breast cancer pathology (Johan Hartman)
summary: Co-led work on an AI model that analyses stained breast tumour tissue to refine grading and split grade 2 tumours into high- and low-risk groups (Annals of Oncology, 2021).
students: Not stated.

sources.label: KI news: AI improves precision in breast cancer diagnosis (2021)

name: AI in mammography screening (Fredrik Strand)
unit: Oncology-Pathology, Karolinska Institutet; Karolinska University Hospital
summary: Studies whether AI can complement or replace radiologists in the first read of screening mammograms, and using AI to choose which women get a supplementary MRI. Uses an in-house AI developed by KTH and KI.
students: Not stated.

sources.label: KI: Using AI to diagnose breast cancer earlier

name: Westman Neuroimaging Group
unit: Division of Clinical Geriatrics, NVS, Karolinska Institutet
summary: Uses MRI, PET and CT with CSF and blood biomarkers to find early markers of Alzheimer's disease, and multivariate machine learning to track disease and treatment. Has an in-house AI that predicts brain age from scans.
students: Not stated.

name: Neuroradiology – MRI physics (Stefan Skare)
summary: Develops motion-robust MRI so awake, moving children can be scanned without anaesthesia. In 2023 the Swedish Childhood Cancer Fund granted SEK 3.9 million to extend this to children with brain and spinal tumours.
students: Not stated.

sources.label: KI news: Skare receives funding from the Childhood Cancer Fund

name: Abdominal and skeletal radiology
summary: Measures organ function and aims to diagnose cancer earlier with better staging and treatment evaluation, with a focus on transplantation and upper abdominal surgery. A skeletal line works on osteoporosis screening with digital radiogrammetry and body composition from CT and MRI.
students: Not stated.

name: Nuclear medicine (Rimma Axelsson)
summary: Hybrid imaging with SPECT/CT and PET/CT for early diagnosis, staging and follow-up in oncology, neurogeriatrics and orthopaedic infection.
students: Not stated.

name: Molecular brain imaging (Andrea Varrone)
summary: Molecular brain imaging of neurodegenerative disorders. Group member Simon Cervenka develops new ways to diagnose and treat psychotic disorders, mainly with PET.
students: Not stated.

name: Karolinska Cardiovascular MR Group
pi: Members include Martin Ugander, Andreas Sigfridsson
unit: Clinical Physiology, Karolinska Institutet and Karolinska University Hospital
summary: Develops new cardiovascular MR imaging approaches and runs translational and clinical studies on heart failure, ischaemic heart disease, myocarditis and cardiac pumping.
students: Not stated.

name: AI ultrasound for ovarian tumours (Elisabeth Epstein)
unit: Clinical Science and Education, Södersjukhuset (KI SÖS)
summary: Runs an AI decision-support platform for ultrasound assessment of ovarian tumours, a Class IIb medical device under EU MDR, in collaboration with Kevin Smith (KTH/SciLifeLab).
students: A research engineer role is open now (see Jobs).

name: aICU: clinical AI in intensive care
pi: Anna Schandl's group (Perioperative and Intensive Care)
unit: Clinical Research and Education, Södersjukhuset (KI SÖS)
summary: Builds data infrastructure and tools to develop, evaluate and eventually test clinical AI prospectively in intensive care, using structured data, high-resolution time series, free text, ECG and radiology data.
students: A research engineer role is open now (see Jobs).

name: Health informatics (Sabine Koch)
summary: Clinical informatics research on patient-centred information systems, decision support and decision making.
students: Not stated.

name: Medical Technology and Digital Health group

summary: Radiation physics for imaging and radiotherapy, radiation protection and nuclear-emergency preparedness, and proton versus photon treatment planning with the Skandion Clinic.
students: Not stated.

name: Institute for International Economic Studies (IIES)
summary: A research institute at Stockholm University, founded in 1962, doing advanced research across a broad range of economics.
students: The page refers to graduate studies and the PhD programme at Stockholm University. No assistant positions are listed.

name: Department of Economics, SSE
summary: Research spanning micro, macro and international economics, using a wide range of theoretical and applied methods.
students: About 35 PhD students; the department runs PhD and Master's programmes. No assistant openings are listed on the page.

name: House of Innovation, SSE
pi: Department of Entrepreneurship, Innovation and Technology
summary: Research projects in management, economics and organisation studies using interviews, surveys, econometrics, experiments, machine learning and text analysis.
students: Recruits research and teaching assistants on a rolling basis (see Jobs).

students: The department offers doctoral studies in public law.

name: Music research at KMH
unit: Royal College of Music in Stockholm
summary: Artistic research in music (interpretation, improvisation, composition, interactivity and human-machine interaction) and music education research drawing on musicology, pedagogy, psychology and sociology.
